entries.gist: Control-room software for running the distribution grid
entries.description: Software platform used by distribution system operators to monitor, control and optimise the distribution grid. It combines SCADA, outage management and analytics such as fault location, isolation and service restoration (FLISR) and volt/VAR optimisation in one system.
entries.note: Like OMS, ADMS is normally bought off the shelf rather than built in-house. The same vendor landscape applies — GE, Oracle, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric and ABB all sell ADMS platforms — since ADMS is typically DMS, OMS and analytics sold together as one integrated product.

entries.gist: Software for operating the distribution network
entries.description: Control-room software for operating the medium- and low-voltage distribution network — switching, load monitoring and network state estimation. An ADMS is a DMS with outage management and advanced analytics added.

entries.gist: System that finds and manages power outages
entries.description: System that detects, locates and manages power outages, typically by combining customer trouble calls, smart meter events and network topology to predict which device has failed and to track restoration.
entries.note: OMS is a category, not one specific product. Utilities buy it off the shelf from vendors such as GE, Oracle, Siemens, Hitachi Energy, Schneider Electric and ABB — either as a standalone system integrated with SCADA and GIS, or bundled as a module inside a broader ADMS platform. Fully custom-built systems exist but are the exception, usually only at very large utilities with unusual requirements.

entries.gist: Real-time monitoring and control of grid equipment
entries.description: Real-time system that collects measurements from substations and field devices and lets operators send control commands, such as opening or closing a breaker. It is the data backbone that DMS, ADMS and EMS sit on top of.

entries.gist: Control-room software for the transmission grid
entries.description: Control-room software for the high-voltage transmission grid — generation dispatch, state estimation, contingency analysis and frequency control. The transmission-level counterpart to a DMS.

entries.gist: Small power source or flexible load on the grid
entries.description: Small-scale power source or flexible load connected to the distribution grid rather than the transmission grid — rooftop solar, batteries, EV chargers, heat pumps and small wind.

entries.gist: Software that controls fleets of DERs
entries.description: Software that monitors, forecasts and controls large numbers of DERs so the grid operator can use them as flexibility — for example curtailing solar or dispatching batteries to relieve a constraint.

entries.gist: The company that runs the local grid
entries.description: The company that owns and operates the local distribution grid and connects end customers. In Norway the DSO is the nettselskap; the transmission grid is operated by the TSO (Statnett).

entries.gist: The company that runs the national grid
entries.description: The operator responsible for the high-voltage transmission grid and for keeping the whole power system in balance. Statnett in Norway.

entries.gist: Smart meters and the network behind them
entries.description: The end-to-end smart metering system — meters, communication network and head-end system — that delivers interval consumption data and meter events to the utility.

entries.fullName: Fault Location, Isolation and Service Restoration
entries.gist: Grid that isolates faults and restores power by itself
entries.description: Automated ADMS function that pinpoints a fault on a feeder, opens switches to isolate the faulted section and closes tie switches to restore supply to unaffected customers, usually within a minute.

entries.gist: Automatic voltage and reactive power control
entries.description: Coordinated control of voltage regulators, capacitor banks and inverters to keep voltage within limits while reducing losses or demand.
